title: Implement a max-heap from scratch in Python
description: Implement MaxHeap with push, pop, peek, and size using sift-up/sift-down on a list. No heapq allowed.

files.tests/test_max_heap.py:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
from src.max_heap import MaxHeap
import pytest


def test_push_pop_order():
    h = MaxHeap()
    for v in [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]:
        h.push(v)
    result = []
    while h.size() > 0:
        result.append(h.pop())
    assert result == [9, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 1]


def test_peek():
    h = MaxHeap()
    h.push(3)
    h.push(7)
    h.push(1)
    assert h.peek() == 7
    assert h.size() == 3  # peek should not remove


def test_size():
    h = MaxHeap()
    assert h.size() == 0
    h.push(10)
    h.push(20)
    h.push(30)
    assert h.size() == 3


def test_empty_raises():
    h = MaxHeap()
    with pytest.raises((IndexError, Exception)):
        h.pop()

task_spec.prompt:
Implement MaxHeap in src/max_heap.py using a list:
- _sift_up(i): while i>0, compare with parent=(i-1)//2; swap and move up if heap[i]>heap[parent]
- _sift_down(i): find largest among i, left=2i+1, right=2i+2; swap with largest child if larger than i; repeat
- push(val): append val, call _sift_up
- pop(): swap root with last, pop last, call _sift_down(0); raise IndexError if empty
- peek(): return _heap[0]; raise IndexError if empty
- size(): return len(_heap)
All 4 tests must pass.
